name: Site deploy on pull request close

pr.title: Deploy the site when a pull request closes
pr.head: bf219ee42776bbd2c988e72d14bac941bb10a242

summary: The Projector site is a GitHub Pages site that a repository's own workflow, .github/workflows/projector-site.yml, builds and deploys. Its Reviews index lists each pull request with a summary and shows whether it is open, merged, or closed. Until now the workflow deployed only when a summary was published, when a push to the default branch changed a watched path, or on demand. A pull request that merged or closed without touching a watched path started no deploy, so the Reviews index kept showing it as open.

This pull request adds a trigger: the workflow now also deploys when a pull request in the repository closes, merged or not. It uses pull_request_target, a GitHub event that runs the default branch's workflow on the default branch, so the deploy is allowed by the github-pages environment and never checks out the pull request's code. A pull request from a fork deploys nothing.

It implements § 2.4 of the proposed-projects plan, which needs this deploy so that a proposed plan leaves the site as soon as its pull request closes. The proposed projects themselves come in later pull requests, so the plan moves to in-progress.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• pull_request_target: a pull request event that GitHub runs from the workflow file on the default branch, with the default branch checked out, rather than on the pull request's merge ref.
  • Concurrency group: a name that GitHub uses to run one workflow run at a time. A newer waiting run replaces an older waiting one in the same group.
  • Workflow shape: the exact text Projector writes for the site workflow, with only the action ref, branch, dispatch event, and watched paths free. current is today's text; earlier is one from PREVIOUS_WORKFLOWS.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:

  • bf219ee takes up the suggestion: the warning and the docs now also name project site workflow --write. Reviewed clean, with no finding threads.

groups.title: The workflow deploys when a pull request closes
groups.kicker: The new trigger, the fork guard, and the fork's own concurrency group
intro: The generated workflow, the WORKFLOW template in summary.py, gains three lines of behavior. Each one answers a separate risk of running on a closed pull request.

1. The trigger. pull_request_target with types: [closed] starts a run for every pull request that closes, merged or not. A plain pull_request trigger would run on refs/pull/<n>/merge, which the github-pages environment refuses, and the site action's checkout would build that pull request's tree as the site.
  2. The fork guard. The publish job's if: runs only when the pull request's head repository is this one. A fork's pull request, or one whose fork was deleted (its head repository is then null), skips the deploy.
  3. The fork's concurrency group. A fork's run takes fork-<run id> instead of pages. Without that, the skipped run would still join pages, where it could replace a real deploy that was waiting.

The permissions stay the four every other run has. This repository's own workflow differs from the template, because it runs the action from main and watches more paths, so it gets the same three changes by hand.

checks.text: No step reads the pull request's code. The site action checks out the default GITHUB_REF and GITHUB_SHA, which on pull_request_target are the default branch. The only event field in use, the head repository's name, appears only in expressions, never in a shell step.

files.note: The new WORKFLOW, the previous one added to PREVIOUS_WORKFLOWS, and workflow_shape, which tells the current shape from an earlier one.

checks.text: The doubled braces render as single ones: workflow_text("v0", "main") produces ${{ … format('fork-{0}', github.run_id) … }}, which test_a_pull_request_in_the_repository_deploys_when_it_closes_and_a_forks_does_not pins.
This entry equals WORKFLOW at the merge base byte for byte, compared directly against git show of the base, so a workflow the previous release wrote is still recognized and rewritten.

The current template is tried before the earlier ones. A file's watched paths are free in both, so a workflow with an older paths list but the new trigger counts as current and gets no warning; project init still rewrites it, because its text differs.

files.note: This repository's own workflow, edited by hand with the same trigger, condition, and concurrency group as the template.

checks.text: When the merge of this pull request starts a run on pull_request_target, the run checks this condition first. A skipped publish job for this repository's own pull request means the condition is wrong.

groups.title: project check warns about an outdated workflow
groups.kicker: A warning that points a repository at the new shape
intro: A repository picks up the new workflow when someone runs project init, which rewrites a workflow Projector wrote and keeps one edited by hand. To tell people that a refresh is due, project check now prints a site-workflow-outdated warning while the workflow is an earlier shape that Projector wrote.

Like the existing instructions warnings, it prints on stderr and never changes the exit code. A hand-edited workflow, such as this repository's, gets no warning, because Projector cannot tell what its owner meant.

files.note: site_workflow_issues reads the workflow, asks workflow_shape for its shape, and returns the warning only for earlier. check appends it to the store's issues.

checks.text: The warning names two fixes. project init rewrites the workflow in most repositories. project site workflow --write is for a repository with site.enabled = false, where init leaves the workflow alone.

files.note: Tests for the trigger, the shapes, project init on every earlier shape, and the warning on every case the plan lists.

checks.text: Ran in the full suite at this head: every earlier shape warns, and the current shape, a hand-edited workflow, and no workflow do not. Every case exits 0.
